sourceNote: The mesh of the user (assets/models/fox/fox.glb, assets/models/fox/README.md), with new quad faces on each arm from the shoulder line to the wrist, and arms 1.21 times longer. The user allowed loop edges, retopology, and extra bones for the arm and wrist twist on 2026-10-24 ("add loop edges and retopology and additional bones if needed to address them"). tools/blender/fox_arms.py replays the Blender session that made it. The faces of the paws, the trunk, the legs, and the head are the faces of the user. The file of the user, fox.glb, stays unchanged.
paintedNote: The weights of the clavicles and the arms are the automatic weights of Blender with the Weight Paint fixes of tools/blender/fox_arms.py. The vertices on the bones of paintedLower (the trunk up to the chest, the neck, the head, the ears, the legs, and the tail) keep the rule weights, as on the wolf and the mouse: the seated bind of the app depends on them.

rootNormals.note: The skin faces whose middle lies within radius (units) of the head of an upper arm take the normals of the skin with no crease angle in the app (root_rim() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py), as on the beaver and the rhino. On the rebuilt arms, the crease angle split the normals at the back of the right armpit of the red fox into a thin dark slit at the tip and a dark wedge in the lift, from the stage camera (az150, elevation 40). The back of the armpit lies 0.094 units from the shoulder joint, and the radius 0.15 gave the same look as 0.12 (docs/research/2026-10-25-fox-arms.md).

armSegments.rootSegmentNote: The rule weight of each upper arm goes to its first segment (segment_joints() and main() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py), so that the trunk around the socket takes the roll of the first ring of the tube: the socket and the trunk beside it keep the rule weights of the config, and the whole roll of the old upper arm bone folded the faces of the socket.
armSegments.note: Each upper arm and each forearm has 4 deform segments, and each elbow and wrist a helper bone of this length in units, which spans the rings of its joint in the bind. The app turns them from the joints of the pose (poseArm() of src/models/studio-rig.ts). They replace the raise shape of the bow arm. The helper is twice the gap of the elbow rings (gap of tools/blender/fox_arms.py), as on the wolf.

name: Fox

app.note: The scale is 1.5504 m for each unit: 1.3 times the scale that puts the standing head top of the fox at 1.083 m, the head top of the parametric fox (docs/research/2026-10-14-fox-mesh/landmark-probe.txt and scale-variants.txt), because the user asked for a fox 1.3 times the size on 2026-10-14 (docs/research/2026-10-14-animal-size.md). The leg factor raises the standing shoulder joint from 0.625 to 0.715 units, so app.shoulders is 1.108536 m, and the scale stays, so that the trunk, the head before its factor, and the arms keep their meters (docs/research/2026-10-14-fox-rabbit-form.md). The user asked for a full violin on 2026-10-14 ("fox and rabbit violin too small"), and the arms reached 0.6036 m (docs/research/2026-10-14-neck-violin.md). Then the user asked for shorter arms with the same violin ("reduce the arm length of the fox and rabbit without changing the violin size"). Of the reaches 0.4901 m, 0.5452 m, and 0.6036 m, the manager chose the middle one, so the reach is 0.5452 m, and the violin stays 0.998 of the violin of the app (docs/research/2026-10-14-arms-rest.md).

armFactorNote: The factor of the upper arm and the forearm in the rig: 1, because the rig with arm segments does not stretch the arms (armSegments of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py). The arms of fox-arms.glb are already 1.21 times longer than the arms of the user mesh (step_shape() of tools/blender/violin_arms.py, called by tools/blender/fox_arms.py), and the arm joints below are the joints of the longer arms, so the reach stays app.reach. The reasons for the factor 1.21 before: pnpm rig-mesh fox --check measured 0.4574 m with no factor at this scale. The factor was 1.0782 before the full violin and 1.35 with it, and the middle factor 1.21 shortens the arms that the user found too long (docs/research/2026-10-14-arms-rest.md). With no --check, pnpm rig-mesh stops when the reach is more than 1% from app.reach.
legFactorNote: The factor of the thigh and the shin. Each one stretches only between its joints, the foot keeps its size, and the body rises 0.09 units, so that the soles stay at y 0. The user asked for longer legs and a higher seat on 2026-10-14, and then said that the legs of the factor 2.0 were too long. The legs gave a seat of 0.235 m (0.164 m before). Since 2026-10-16, the chair of the app fits the legs (no seat of ANIMALS), so the soles stand on the floor. Since 2026-10-17, the thighs 25 degrees down and the vertical shins give a seat of 0.270 m (0.219 m with the thighs 15 degrees down and the slanted shins of 2026-10-16, docs/research/2026-10-17-fox-form.md). The factor 3.25 gave the seat of the reference fox, about one visible head (0.484 m), with a standing fox of 2.23 m (docs/research/2026-10-14-fox-rabbit-form.md).
headFactorNote: The factor of the head and the ears around the neck joint. The weights blend the growth over the neck. The user asked for a larger head that appears cuter on 2026-10-14, and then said that the head of the factor 1.5 was too big. With 1.25, a thin face between the neck and the head turned over when the head turned, and the fox folded in 15.0% of the play samples. The factors 1.2 and 1.3 gave 3.3% and 6.5% (docs/research/2026-10-14-fox-rabbit-form/rig-mesh-check-fox-head-variants.log). The export keeps the head height and the head center of the head before the factor for the holds (ungrown() of tools/studio-body.ts).
neckFactorNote: The factor of the length of the neck between the neck joint and the head joint. The neck shortens only between its joints, and the head and the ears keep their size and move down the neck with the head joint. The export moves the head center of the holds with the head (headRig() of tools/studio-body.ts). The user said "fox neck too long" on 2026-10-14. Of the factors 0.8, 0.65, and 0.5 (the head 2.2, 3.9, and 5.6 cm down), the manager chose the middle one (docs/research/2026-10-14-neck-violin.md). The user said "the cat and fox's necks are too long" on 2026-10-16, and the manager chose the next step, 0.5: the neck joint is 5.6 cm from the head joint (7.3 cm with 0.65), and the chin is 0.247 H above the shoulder joints (0.288 H, docs/decisions/2026-10-17-fox-form.md).
jointsNote: The places are in the units and the axes of the studio in the pose of the source: 1 unit from the soles to the ear tips, the soles at y = 0, +z forward, +x the left side. The right side mirrors the left side. The probes are in docs/research/2026-10-14-fox-mesh/. sections.py gives the cuts at each height: the feet below y 0.05 (the toes forward to z 0.14), the thin shins from 0.05 to 0.11, the wide thighs from 0.13 to the crotch at 0.23, the body from 0.23 to 0.51 (x ±0.093 under the arms), the shoulders at 0.53 to 0.66, the narrow neck at 0.69 to 0.71 (x ±0.089), the head from 0.71 with the muzzle to z 0.28, and the ears apart from 0.91. The trunk joints lie 0.01 to 0.02 behind the middle of the body cut, as in the rabbit, from the hips over the crotch to the chest 0.085 below the shoulder joint. The thigh joint lies at the crotch on the middle of the leg cut, the knee where the thin shin meets the wide thigh, the ankle where the foot starts, and the toes at the ball of the foot. The ear joint lies on the line of the middles of the ear cuts at 0.91 and 0.95, at the top of the head (0.89), and its tail at the ear tip. The cuts at x 0.101 to 0.221 give the middle line of the free arm (sections-x.txt), which leaves the body between x 0.081 and 0.101. The shoulder joint lies on that line, 0.03 inside the root (x 0.07). The wrist lies at the narrow cut where the paw starts (arm-axis.txt, s 0.01 to 0.02), the elbow halfway from the shoulder joint to the wrist and 0.01 behind the line, and the finger joint at the knuckles, 0.03 before the tip of the paw. The tail is a chain of two bones (tail_line.py, tail-line.txt). The tail joint lies at the middle of the root of the tail, between its top on the back (y 0.42, z -0.09) and its bottom on the thighs (y 0.26, z -0.055). The tail_tip joint lies at the bend of the middle line of the tail cuts, where the tail leaves the body (y 0.25, z -0.15), 0.117 units from the root, and its tail at the tip of the tail (y 0.01, z -0.247). Each roll is the hint of the z axis of the bone, forward by default. The arm bones take the normal of the palm (palm): the smallest principal direction of the vertices of the left paw, inward and back (facts.txt). Since 2026-10-25, the joints of the elbow, the forearm twist, the wrist, and the paw are the joints of the arms that are 1.21 times longer (fox_arms.py), and the joints of the source arms are in source_joints() of tools/blender/violin_arms.py.

studio.trunkNote: The trunk of the seated bind sits upright (trunk_turn() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py): the pelvis turns back around the head of the hips until the hip angle from the side opens by open degrees, and each trunk bone takes its share of that turn as its world turn. With open 3, the trunk axis from the hip joints to the neck joint is vertical within 1 degree in the play pose (2.7 degrees forward before), as seated string players sit tall and do not lean on the chair back (docs/decisions/2026-10-16-hip-open.md). The user first chose a recline toward the chair back, and then asked for a straight back on 2026-10-16. The shares fall from the spine1 to the head in equal steps, so that the four joints from the spine to the head share the counter turn, and the head stays level. Of the shares that pnpm rig-mesh fox --check --roles fox-violinist,flutist --step 1 tried at open 20, these folded the red fox in 9.1% and the tan fox in 0.7% of the play samples (1.5% and 0.6% on main). The chest 0.667, the neck 0.333, and the head 0 folded the red fox in 14.8%. Each share set with a head share above 0 folded the tan fox in 92% to 100%: face 1034 at the back of the neck turns over when the flute hold turns the head. The haunch and the root of the tail rise onto the seat top of the upright body (seat_lift()). The value 0 keeps the trunk of the source.
studio.note: The studio has no fox. The seat is the seat of a long thigh: legTurns gives the world turn of each left leg bone from the seated bind pose to the source, and the right side mirrors it. The thigh slopes 25 degrees down from the hip to the knee, 8 degrees out, so that the hips are above the knees, as seated string players sit, and the shin is vertical, with the ankle under the knee, so that the knee angle from the side is 115 degrees (docs/research/2026-10-16-hip-open/leg_turns.py <config> 25 8 0). The user asked for a taller chair and legs more perpendicular to the floor on 2026-10-16, and the manager chose 25 degrees of the mock of 20, 25, and 30 degrees (docs/decisions/2026-10-17-fox-form.md). The thigh of 2026-10-16 sloped 15 degrees down, and the shin slanted 23.8 degrees forward (docs/decisions/2026-10-16-hip-open.md). The foot and the toes keep the turn of the source, so that the soles stand flat on the floor. The seat of the studio rabbit turned the thigh 57 degrees, and the long thigh of the fox stood almost upright on the chair. The bind arms are the bind arms of the studio rabbit (tools/mesh-rigs/rabbit.json, docs/research/2026-10-13-rabbit-mesh/studio-targets.ts): the unit direction of each left arm bone in the bind pose. tailBind gives the direction of each tail bone in the seated bind pose: the root goes back over the seat, 7 degrees below the level, and the tip hangs back and down behind the chair, 54 degrees below the level. Then the tail goes at most 0.0005 units over the seat top, and its lowest point is 0.038 units above the soles.

weights.stretchRampNote: With a ramp, the upper arm stretches by the arm factor only on the free arm: the share of the stretch fades from 0 to 1 over this many units on each side of the plane |x| = armSplit. 0 gives no ramp. With the arm factor 1.35 and the hold of the neck round, the ramp of 0.02 folded the faces of the trunk below the right armpit in 20.9% of the play samples, and 29.7% with no ramp (docs/research/2026-10-14-neck-violin.md). With the later holds, the ramp folds more: with the hold of main, 14.2% against 9.9% with no ramp (docs/research/2026-10-14-rig-retro.md), and with the arm factor 1.21 and the fitted hold, 15.7% against 12.8% (docs/research/2026-10-14-arms-rest/rig-mesh-check-fox-ramp.log). The rabbit has no ramp either.

sliver.note: The corners of each thin face share one set of weights, so that the face moves rigidly and does not turn over at a bent joint. A thin face has a corner angle below angle (degrees) and a longest edge below longest (units). The values are the values of the rabbit.

line.note: The middle corner of each long thin face (a corner angle above angle, in degrees) takes the mix of the weights of its two other corners by its place along their line, so that it does not lag behind the line when a joint bends. With head, the corners of the head take the rule too. A thin face of the jaw (corner angle 172 degrees, 5 cm long) and a thin face under the chin (153 degrees) folded in 35% and 9% of the play samples when the head turned against the neck, and with this rule in none (pnpm fold-probe fox-violinist).

weights.clavicleFromNote: The share of the clavicle weight that a vertex keeps grows from 0 at the lower height to 1 at the upper height (units), and the chest takes the rest. Bone heat gave a small face of the right chest (y 0.57) a clavicle weight of 0.07 on one corner and the spine on the others. The bow arm turns the right clavicle far, so the face turned over in 76% of the play samples. The clavicle joint is at y 0.635.
weights.armTopNote: The share of the weight of the clavicles and of the upper arms that a vertex keeps falls from 1 at the lower height to 0 at the upper height (units), and the neck takes the rest. The shoulders end at y 0.66 and the neck is narrowest at 0.69 to 0.71. Bone heat gave a vertex of the side of the neck 0.33 of the right clavicle and 0.24 of the right upper arm, and a raised bow arm dragged them.
weights.shoulderHeadNote: Below headFrom, the share of the head weight that goes to the neck grows from 0 at the smaller distance from the middle plane to all at the larger distance (units). The values are the values of the rabbit, scaled by the neck of the fox (x ±0.089 against ±0.077).
weights.fingersNote: The fingers keep this share of their bone heat weight, and the hand takes the rest, as in the rabbit.

haunch.note: The part of the thigh weight that goes to the hips grows from 0 at the lower height to 1 at the upper height, so that the buttocks stay on the hips and the long thigh turns onto the seat. With the ramp of the first config (0.11 to 0.185), the upper half of the thigh stayed upright. With the ramp from 0.2 to 0.27, 9 faces of the hip crease turned over in the seated bind, and with this ramp none.

weights.note: Beyond the plane |x| = armSplit, only the free arm follows the arm bones: the cuts of sections.py x show the arm apart from the body from x 0.101 out. Above headFrom, each vertex except the ears follows the head only: the neck is narrowest at y 0.69 to 0.71, and the cheek fur starts at 0.73. Each ear vertex goes to its ear bone with a ramp over the heights of earBase. The tail has two bones (tail): the vertices within radius of the line from the root over the bend to the tip, and behind the plane z = behind, follow the tail bones. The share of the tail bones grows from 0 to 1 over the places of root along the line (units from the root), the share of the tip within the tail grows from 0 to 1 over bend units on each side of the bend, and the share of the tail bones takes the mean of its neighbors in smooth rounds, so that the root has no hard edge. The radius holds the widest cut of the tail (x Â±0.103 at y 0.21), and the plane keeps the backs of the thighs (z -0.04 at y 0.21) out of it.

refine.ringsNote: The first config has no rings. pnpm rig-mesh fox --check lists the thin faces near the joints as candidates for a ring (check.thin).

flip.note: The long edge of a face of the arms with a corner angle above angle (degrees) in the seated bind mesh flips to the corner of the face on its other side, when the two faces lie almost on one plane (normals, degrees) and the surface moves at most move (units). The values are the values of the rabbit.

check.note: pnpm rig-mesh --check lists the faces of the seated bind mesh with a corner angle below angle (degrees) and a longest edge of at least length (units), when that edge passes within near (units) of a joint of the arms or the legs. These faces are candidates for a ring (refine.rings). The values are the values of the rabbit.

shift.note: The orange fur moves in Oklch (shift_colors() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py). A fur face takes the move by the smoothstep of its chroma from 0.06 to 0.1 and of its lightness from 0.35 to 0.45: the orange faces of the texture have the chroma 0.14 to 0.16, and the faces between the orange and the white fur 0.06 to 0.13. The white belly and muzzle (chroma 0.03 to 0.04), the black legs and ear backs (lightness 0.16 to 0.32), and the gloss eyes and nose keep their colors. The user asked for a redder fox like the reference on 2026-10-19. Of the half step, the full step, and the step past the reference, the manager rule took the full step, nearest to the reference: the lightness 0.745 times, the chroma 1.21 times, and the hue 12 degrees toward red. The orange fur of four fox heads in the play frame then has the Oklch lightness 0.655, chroma 0.125, and hue 43.1 degrees, against 0.651, 0.139, and 43.4 in orchestra-latest.png, and 0.844, 0.107, and 63.8 before. The sRGB gamut limits the chroma of the darker orange (docs/research/2026-10-19-fox-red.md).

colors.note: Each face takes the mean sRGB color of the texture at the samples of a grid of the given steps on the face. A face is dark when its share of samples with a linear luminance below dark is at least eyeShare, and then it takes the mean of its dark samples. Each other face takes the mean of its samples that are not dark. A dark face in the eye box (the left eye at x 0.043, y 0.805 in the front view, mirrored for the right eye) is a face of an eye. A face in the nose box whose color is nearer to the nose color than to white is a face of the nose: the nose of the fox is black, at the tip of the muzzle (y 0.765, z 0.28). The box starts above the dark faces of the mouth (y 0.736 to 0.75), which the first box held. Then each face takes the nearest color of a palette of palette colors, from k-means in Oklab. Last, shift moves the orange fur of the texture to the red-orange of the reference foxes.

eyeShell.note: Each eye shell is a fan from the middle of the dark faces of the eye to at most this number of points of their edge, lifted this far (units) along the normal of the eye. pnpm studio-body finds each eye by its fan, drops the fan, and the app puts its pea eye there (design 4.5). The old eye is the dark faces and each face whose middle lies within reach times the radius of their edge, seen along the normal of the eye: the white of the almond eye and the brown lid shading under the right eye lie within 0.24 to 0.70 of that radius. After the palette, the faces of the old eye take the color with the largest area in the ring of faces that share a corner with it, so that no outline of the old eye shows around the pea eye. Then each patch of dark faces (the faces that share corners) that no old eye holds, with its middle within darkReach times the radius of the edge and within half the radius of its plane, takes the color with the largest area in the ring of faces that share a corner with the patch. The dark face 1.67 radii up and in from the middle of the left eye, the end of the black upper lid line of the almond eye, lies within darkReach. The values of lift and points are the values of the rabbit.

chair.note: The chair is wider than the chair of the rabbit rig, because the haunch of the fox is x ±0.17. The seat is level, and its top is the lowest point of the seated body over the seat, with no shin, foot, or tail. Its front edge ends where the thighs, which slope down, leave the seat top at the haunch: the seat top stays for the front edges from 0.03 to 0.05 units, and with the front edge 0.01 units further forward, it fell 0.6 cm under the thighs (front-scan-fox.txt of docs/research/2026-10-17-fox-form/). So the seat of the app is 0.287 m deep. The back edge lies 0.0258 units (4 cm) forward of the back edge of 2026-10-16 (-0.16 units), so that the body keeps its place 1 cm in front of the back posts (the user said "let the fox and rabbit sit in more" on 2026-10-16), and the seat of the app ends at the front edge of this chair (no seatBack in ANIMALS).

crease.note: The seated bind is smoothed across the crease where the belly meets the top of each thigh (crease_relax() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py). The user said "there's an obvious fold/gap between the trunk and the thigh, can that be made less obvious?" on 2026-10-16. The cause is the geometry: the upright trunk over the sloped thighs folds the mesh there, the faces of the fold face away from the light, and the render with a flat light and the face colors shows no line (docs/research/2026-10-16-hip-open.md). The seam is each vertex of both a trunk face and a thigh face, up to back units behind the hip joints and above below units under them, and the region adds rings rings of neighbors. Each vertex moves share of the way to the middle of its neighbors in rounds rounds, with a weight that falls from the seam out. Of 3, 8, and 20 rounds, the middle one is the moderate step. The corrective shapes give the source back, so the standing body keeps its form.

sit.note: The underside of the haunch behind the hip joints goes down onto the seat in the seated bind (sit() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py), because the buttocks of the mesh curve up behind the hip joints. The manager found the back of the haunch 3 to 11 cm above the seat on 2026-10-14. The drop of each vertical line over the seat is its gap less gap, at most most, and it fades over ramp units before the hip joints and over the last end units of the haunch. The drops take the mean of their neighbors in smooth rounds on a grid of step units, and each vertex moves by the drop less its height above the underside, to 0 at band units. The side view of the underside is 10.5 cm above the seat at most before, and 1.4 cm after. With a band of 0.1 units, a face of the right side of the haunch turned over (docs/research/2026-10-14-fox-rabbit-fix.md). With the thighs 25 degrees down of 2026-10-17, the root of the tail kept the side view of the final bind 2.57 cm above the seat (2.37 cm with the thighs of 2026-10-16). The vertices of the root of the tail share their weight with the hips, so with root, the tail share of a vertex counts only by its smoothstep from 0.7 to 0.95, the root moves with the haunch, as for the cat, and the side view of the final bind is 0.35 cm above the seat at most (docs/research/2026-10-17-fox-form.md). The corrective shapes give the source back, so the standing body keeps its form.

smooth.note: The fur spikes at the bottom of the back of the head hang over the back of the neck, and with the head factor 1.2 and the neck factor 0.65 they made a dark jagged band under the head from the back and the sides (the manager on 2026-10-14). The band shows also with the factors 1 (docs/research/2026-10-14-fox-rabbit-fix.md), so the rig smooths the source inside the box before the growth: the back of the neck and the bottom of the back of the head (x from -0.11 to 0.11, y from 0.66 to 0.78, behind z 0.03). The muzzle, the jaw, the eyes, the cheek fur at the sides, and the ears stay outside the box. Each vertex inside moves 0.5 of the way to the middle of its neighbors in 12 rounds, at most 0.035 units. The spikes set the back of the box of the head, so the smoothing moves the head center of the holds 0.011 units (1.71 cm) forward, and with it the violin. The violin box then came nearer to the stands and the neighbors, and the stages of four demos grew by 0.2% to 4.6%. The rig writes the move back into the file (head_shift()), and the export keeps the head center of the head before the smoothing, so the holds, the footprints, and the stages keep their places (docs/research/2026-10-15-fox-rig2.md).
